items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: we engaged a clarinetist named Eddie Williams and on th e following Tuesday night, we went to the Stable to do the audition.

ctx.x: But things were going along nicely at the rehersals and one day, I think that Timmie or Inez hit the numbers for five cents and decided to have a little party for the band. Timmie had been speaking about a famous dish he used to cook called Danish meat balls, or fish balls, and he cooked some for the party. They were made with fish and mixed with mashed potatoes and served with a white sauce, and they were very tasty, to my surprise.

After two months rehersing, Timmie told us that the next week we would have an audition at Kelly's Stable, which was well known jazz spot on 52nd Street between 6th and 7th Avenue. Kelly's Stable was a jazz club long before the Famous Door and a few other 52nd Steret joints became famous. The next rehersal, Franz Jackson did not show up, and the one after that, also. We had no idea what had happened to him, so we engaged a clarinetist named Eddie Williams and on th e following Tuesday night, we went to the Stable…

Generally an audition was done in the afternoon, but the two owners of Kelly's Stable whom I only knew as George and Nick, wanted us to audition when there were people in the place, in order to obtain the reaction of the public to our playing. There were two other orchestras auditioning that night and one of them was under the name of Franz Jackson. He had pulled a dirty trick on me by accepting to play with me until he found out where and for whom the audition would be, and then form his own group and undermine…
